- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after a recent spike or correction.
- Overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices are rising sharply or showing momentum.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in upward trends — model reacts slower than actual market dynamics.
- Shows overconfidence in short-term reversals; frequently forecasts sharp drops after a spike, but prices often continue rising or stabilize.
- Underestimates mean reversion in the middle of the forecast — fails to account for price volatility clustering or momentum decay.
- Overestimates volatility in the final days when prices are trending upward — model assumes correction or peak is near, but prices keep rising.
- When true prices are rising steadily, model often flattens or slightly declines in the middle of the forecast, missing the continuation.
- Model is sensitive to recent low prices — tends to overcorrect upward when recent prices are near a bottom, leading to premature peaks.
- Forecasts often peak too early in the horizon — especially when true prices are still rising or consolidating.
- Underestimates the impact of policy or supply-side shocks — model fails to adjust for sudden regulatory changes or supply disruptions.
